Point 3 of the algorithmic review recorded on roll-lqjj.14 remains present on main cdf311f1af0c6066bd6bef32f9540d034312f45d, checked against fetched origin/main on 2026-10-15. No existing implementation task covers it.

Evidence: crates/beadroll-core/src/replay/apply/create.rs:48 retains every uid in State::awaiting on every create and calls materialise_dangling for each waiting issue. materialise_dangling (:166) scans all of that issue's remaining unresolved dependencies. State::awaiting is still a Vec<EventId> (state.rs:108). Skipping issues with no unresolved dependencies helps the ordinary case but leaves quadratic work when every create adds another issue with a missing target, even when no awaited key arrives.

The original release probes on roll-lqjj.14 measured 8,000/16,000 creates with one unresolved dependency each at 3.02/12.36 seconds, versus 10/23 milliseconds without unresolved dependencies. These are historical measurements from 2026-10-13, not measurements rerun during this investigation.

Index waiting dependencies by their target key so a create visits only the matching work. Consider edge-level indexing or an equivalent arrangement so one issue awaiting many different keys does not have all its remaining dependencies scanned for every arriving key. Preserve the existing binding semantics: actual assigned keys after collision renaming, self references left unresolved, normalized dependency types, imported metadata, import-create tags, and removals by key/type or target uid with their causal rules. Hash iteration must not affect observable order.

The index must remain correct through full replay, projection extension, and projection encode/decode. Relevant seams include replay/apply.rs:240 (dep_remove) and projection/state_codec.rs:72,111 (awaiting persistence). Follow the crate's projection encoding rules if stored representation changes; format 1 and replay outcomes stay unchanged. Existing coverage includes hardening::v4_dangling_replay_determinism, hardening::g14_key_retraction_lost_to_concurrent_target, and projection::tests::finished.

This is separate from the completed import-planning lookup optimization roll-lqjj.15 and projection finishing optimization roll-lqjj.17.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- Unrelated creates do not scan all waiting issues or unresolved edges; resolving many different keys on one issue does not repeatedly scan its entire unresolved list.
- Differential coverage preserves edges, dangling entries, metadata and output order for forward targets, duplicate/multi-type references, self references, key collisions and both forms of retraction, including concurrent target creation. Full replay, extended projections and decoded projections agree.
- Record reproducible release-mode before/after measurements at 8,000 and 16,000 issues for never-arriving targets, targets arriving later, and a single issue awaiting many keys; include the no-unresolved-dependency control. Demonstrate removal of the quadratic scan without wall-clock test gates.
- Update the review decision and findings ledger, plus user-facing guarantees if affected; the fast baseline is green and the change is on main.
fields.title: Index unresolved imported dependencies by the key they await

fields.description:
Point 4 of the algorithmic review recorded on roll-lqjj.14 remains present on main cdf311f1af0c6066bd6bef32f9540d034312f45d, checked against fetched origin/main on 2026-10-15. No existing implementation task covers it.

Evidence: crates/beadroll-core/src/query.rs:202 open_blockers allocates and sorts a complete blocker list and walks ancestors for each issue. is_blocked (:235) calls it just to test emptiness, and State::ready (:242) repeats that for every candidate. The CLI has its own ready path in crates/beadroll/src/commands/list.rs:90-113, so optimizing State::ready alone would leave the command unchanged. commands/queries.rs:14-33 filters blocked issues through is_blocked and then constructs the blocker lists again; view.rs:131 also asks for the boolean in every detail.

The original release probes on roll-lqjj.14 measured a 2,000/4,000-issue parent chain at 407/1,678 milliseconds. These are historical measurements from 2026-10-13, not measurements rerun during this investigation.

Compute and reuse a cycle-aware boolean analysis for one immutable State/query batch, with work approaching O(N+D) before result sorting. Keep full blocker enumeration for callers that display the actual blockers; its output size can itself be large. Wire both public-core and CLI bulk callers through the shared analysis without changing readiness rules or making a single-issue query unnecessarily costly.

Semantic constraints from open_blockers: direct blocks targets count only when not done; disputed closed/tombstone statuses are not done; only an epic waits for its own unfinished direct children. Ancestor inheritance carries prerequisites, not an ancestor's epic-child waiting rule or merely its status. Traversal stops at done ancestors, follows every parent link, excludes revisiting the queried issue, and terminates on merged cycles without recursion overflow. Scope restricts membership only: an outside prerequisite or second parent still blocks an inside issue. Preserve claim/status filtering, result order and CLI limits.

Existing tests in commands/ready_subtree.rs, commands/deep_tree_review4.rs, and core replay/readiness coverage provide compatibility anchors. Keep the reverse-dependency rendering optimization in point 5 independently actionable.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- State::ready and the CLI ready path share analysis across candidates; bulk boolean consumers reuse it where applicable. Boolean checks do not build complete blocker lists per issue.
- Differential tests against the existing blocker semantics cover deep chains, shared/multiple parents, merged parent cycles, done and disputed ancestors/targets, epic versus non-epic children, inherited prerequisites, claims and blockers outside a scoped subtree. Blocker-list contents/order and ready output/filter/limit behavior stay unchanged.
- Record reproducible release-mode before/after measurements on 2,000/4,000 and larger parent chains plus a shared-ancestor graph, excluding fixture setup. Show graph analysis no longer grows quadratically; distinguish analysis from result sorting and required blocker-list output. Timing is evidence, not a test gate.
- Update the review decision and findings ledger, plus user-facing guarantees if affected; the fast baseline is green and the change is on main.
fields.title: Share cycle-aware readiness analysis across issues

fields.description:
Point 5 of the algorithmic review recorded on roll-lqjj.14 remains present on main cdf311f1af0c6066bd6bef32f9540d034312f45d, checked against fetched origin/main on 2026-10-15. No existing implementation task covers it.

Evidence: crates/beadroll-core/src/view.rs:201 dependents iterates every issue, collects and sorts its dependency keys, then filters for the requested issue uid. detail (:97) invokes this for every issue. Multi-issue callers still repeat detail: commands/show.rs:18-20, commands/update.rs:106-110, and commands/ownership.rs:151-155 (claim/takeover results). The child index only handles parent-child relationships and does not replace this all-types reverse lookup.

The original release probes on roll-lqjj.14 measured all details on a sparse graph of 4,000/8,000 issues at 540/2,328 milliseconds. These are historical measurements from 2026-10-13, not measurements rerun during this investigation.

Build a reverse-dependency index once per state snapshot or detail batch and reuse it for requested issues. Preserve dependents in source-issue replay order, with each source's matching edges in sorted-edge order. Retain one output per distinct (target uid, dependency type), all dependency types and statuses, the existing treatment of empty/removed tags and unresolved targets, and the current field/JSON ordering. Index by stable uid so key collisions/renames cannot misdirect edges. Output remains in the caller's requested issue order, including duplicate requests and existing error behavior.

Choose an ephemeral batch view or maintained derived index based on measured cost; no public event-format or ownership-protocol change is needed. Avoid making single-detail calls cost more than their existing one pass, and retain the core detail API's established behavior for consumers. If an index is persisted, follow projection encoding and rebuild rules. Point 4's readiness analysis is a separate bottleneck within detail and must not be conflated with the reverse-dependency measurement.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- Multi-issue show, update and claim/takeover result construction build/reuse the reverse index once per state snapshot, rather than scanning and sorting all issues' dependency edges for every requested detail.
- Equality tests preserve detail objects and their ordering for replay order differing from uid/key order, multiple types between the same pair, duplicate tags, removed edges, dangling dependencies, closed/deleted sources, renamed keys, duplicate requested ids and relevant CLI errors. Existing public single-detail behavior remains compatible.
- Record reproducible release-mode before/after sparse-graph measurements at 4,000 and 8,000 issues for all details, with fixture setup excluded and a single-detail control. Use a graph without ancestor walks to isolate reverse lookup; demonstrate one graph pass plus matching-edge/output work rather than one pass per detail. Timing is evidence, not a test gate.
- Update the review decision and findings ledger, plus user-facing guarantees if affected; the fast baseline is green and the change is on main.
fields.title: Reuse a reverse-dependency index when rendering multiple issue details

data.text:
Reinvestigated all five candidates on 2026-10-15 against clean main cdf311f1af0c6066bd6bef32f9540d034312f45d, which matches fetched origin/main.

1. Addressed by closed roll-lqjj.15: import.rs builds created_keys and resolves dependencies through hash lookups; planning and dry-run validation share resolves. Ledger Z01 and import compatibility tests document the change.
2. Addressed by closed roll-lqjj.17: transition still requests state between closes, but Projection::extend calls finish_some, which skips labels and child-index rebuilding for closes, and advance inserts new ids into a BTreeSet without sorting the full history. Ledger Z02/V01/V02, projection::tests::finished and timing --extend cover this. The documented whole child-index rebuild for a create or dependency change remains an accepted separate limit.
3. Still present: every create scans State::awaiting and every waiting issue's dangling dependencies. Filed roll-lqjj.18.
4. Still present: is_blocked builds open_blockers and repeats ancestor walks across candidates, including the separate CLI ready path. Filed roll-lqjj.19.
5. Still present: detail calls dependents, which scans/sorts dependency edges across every issue, once per requested detail. Multi-show, update and ownership output repeat it. Filed roll-lqjj.20.

All three follow-ups are open P2 tasks under roll-lqjj, with current code references, preserved semantics, behavioral and release-probe acceptance criteria. The performance numbers in their descriptions are explicitly attributed to this original 2026-10-13 review; they were not rerun during this investigation. No repository files changed.

Baseline ./check.sh on the unmodified checkout: 862 tests run, 860 passed, 2 failed, 3 skipped; doctests passed (0 cases), all 14 infra tests passed. Both failures reproduce in a targeted rerun: commands::review6::git_helper::f15_timeout_reaps_the_git_helper (commands/review6/git_helper.rs:65) and hardening::v1_run_git_timeout_hygiene::timeouts_leak_nothing_and_reap_as_documented (beadroll-git/tests/git/hardening/v1_run_git_timeout_hygiene.rs:99). Both assertions concern helper processes remaining after timeout. Log: target/check/tests.log. This investigation did not modify or diagnose the timeout implementation.

Implemented on local main (not pushed) in e364de1, 1439239, 68b93e0 and be67b21, reviewed by Codex over cdf311f..be67b21. State::awaiting (state/awaiting.rs) lists every waiting imported dependency by the key it names, its issue and a number fixed when its list began to wait: a create takes the entries its key settles and visits nothing else, a removal by key finds an issue's entries the same way, an entry taken out holds its place as null until the finishing pass (finish / finish_some) makes the list whole, and survivors are never listed again. The index is derived (projection::ENCODING 4; a state read back numbers each list afresh). Replay outcomes are unchanged: projection::tests::awaiting has scenarios for forward targets, duplicate and multi-type references, self references, a rename beside a removal in the same batch, removals by key and by target, and concurrent target creation, each through replay, extension one record at a time with and without read-back, and one batch, plus a digest of 30 seeded histories pinned from cdf311f's replay; all of them also pass on cdf311f. cargo xtask timing --dangling N, back to back at 8,000 / 16,000: never-arriving 4.50 / 30.28 s -> 0.044 / 0.093 s; arriving later 2.02 / 7.94 s -> 0.038 / 0.084 s; one issue awaiting all 1.57 / 9.05 s -> 0.24 / 0.78 s; control 0.021 / 0.045 s -> 0.019 / 0.046 s; the same issue's keys taken one create a batch by a projection 1.26 / 5.08 s -> 0.38 / 1.52 s. Review round 1 found F1 (ledger W01): entries listed by place were re-listed on every batch (10.13 / 50.68 s on that last shape); fixed in be67b21. Round 2: no findings. ./check.sh green (878 passed, 3 skipped), fmt and clippy clean. The one-issue shapes still grow as N squared because an issue's edges are a VecMap searched in order (roll-dih8.11), filed as a follow-up.

fields.description: Found while closing roll-lqjj.18, measured on main at be67b21 (local) on 2026-10-15. Issue::dep_tags is a VecMap (crates/beadroll-core/src/state/small.rs, roll-dih8.11) searched in order, so each new edge (replay::apply::create::bind for an import, at its create or as a waited-for key arrives, and dep_add) scans the issue's edges, and replay::finish_some's parent-child index rebuild walks them again each batch. cargo xtask timing --dangling N measures it: one issue given every other's key at once (one_has_many) took 0.141 s at 8,000 and 0.498 s at 16,000, the same before and after roll-lqjj.18; one issue waiting for every other's key took 0.24 s and 0.78 s after it; an experiment that left the edge insertion out brought the latter to 0.034 s and 0.066 s. The representation was chosen because an issue mostly has a few edges (roll-dih8.11, heap budget), so a fix must keep the small case's memory: for example a VecMap that builds a lookup once it grows past a threshold, for dep_tags or for every VecMap.
fields.acceptance_criteria:
- Adding the N-th edge to one issue costs less than a scan of its edges once an issue has many, for bind and dep_add alike; edges keep their order and metadata, and replay, extended and decoded projections agree.
- cargo xtask timing --dangling N shows one_has_many and one_awaits_many growing about linearly from 8,000 to 16,000, before and after recorded; the replay heap budget at 200,000 events (timing --replay) still holds.
- docs/REVIEWING.md section 2 and docs/FINDINGS.md updated; the fast baseline is green.
fields.title: One issue given N dependency edges costs N squared: its edges are a vector searched in order

data.reason: A create now visits only the imported dependencies waiting for its own key, and a removal by key only an issue's entries for that key: State::awaiting lists each waiting entry by key, issue and a number it keeps, and a list made whole after a batch lists nothing again (Z03; review finding W01 fixed). Replay outcomes are unchanged, as the scenario tests and a 30-history digest that also pass on cdf311f show; extended and decoded projections agree with replay. Projection ENCODING is 4. Back to back at 16,000: never-arriving keys 30.28 s -> 0.093 s, arriving later 7.94 s -> 0.084 s, one issue awaiting all 9.05 s -> 0.78 s, control 0.045 s -> 0.046 s. The remaining N-squared growth of one issue's N edges is its VecMap (follow-up roll-lqjj.21). Commits e364de1..be67b21 on local main, not pushed; ./check.sh green; Codex review converged in round 2.

data.text: Implemented on main as three commits, be67b21..6abf4ea: ad3efe8 (State::readiness judges every issue at once; State::ready, the CLI's ready, blocked and prime ask it once; State::is_blocked stops at the first thing found; open_blockers unchanged; differential tests replay::readiness and commands::shared_readiness), a47eab4 (cargo xtask timing --ready N), 6abf4ea (REVIEWING §2 decision, FINDINGS Z04, GUARANTEES known limit, CHANGELOG). Verification on this checkout, Rust 1.99.0: cargo fmt --check and clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; ./check.sh green (892 tests passed, 3 skipped, doctests and 14 infra tests passed). Release probe (fastest of 3, 64 cores): held chain analysis 0.9/1.8/4.3/11.2 ms at 2k/4k/8k/16k issues vs complete lists per issue 0.43/1.74/7.12/33.3 s; free chain ready (with sort) 0.4/0.8/2.3/10.4 ms vs analysis 0.2/0.5/0.9/4.6 ms; lattice analysis 1.0/2.0/5.9/13.7 ms vs lists 0.63/2.62/12.6/90.2 s. End to end on a scratch store against the base's bead (best of 5; 3 at 16k): chain-4000 ready 2.05 -> 0.037 s, blocked 4.05 -> 2.14 s (the lists it prints), prime 2.04 -> 0.035 s; lattice-4000 ready 3.59 -> 0.046 s; chain-16000 ready 37.0 -> 0.149 s, blocked 76.5 -> 35.4 s; show and list unchanged. Codex review (gpt-6-astra, xhigh, read-only) of the pinned range reported no actionable defects. Not pushed: the commits are on local main only.

fields.title: Name timing --dangling N in the cargo xtask usage text

fields.notes: Discovered from roll-lqjj.19 while adding timing --ready N. The USAGE text in xtask/src/main.rs lists every timing mode (--replay, --sync, --read, --merge, --contend, --import, --plan, --extend, --ready, --load) but not --dangling N, which roll-lqjj.18 added to timing.rs, the module doc and xtask/AGENTS.md without a usage line or a description sentence. Acceptance: USAGE gains a 'timing --dangling N [--label NAME] [--out FILE]' line and a sentence saying what it measures, matching the module doc of xtask/src/timing/dangling.rs; cargo xtask help shows it. Low severity, documentation only.

data.reason: Readiness is judged once for every issue: State::readiness (crates/beadroll-core/src/query/readiness.rs) finds the issues that are not done and have a prerequisite of their own, then everything not done that reaches one through parents that are not done, by one walk down the parent-child index; State::ready and the CLI's ready, blocked and prime ask it once a command, State::is_blocked stops at the first thing found, and open_blockers still lists the blockers for bead blocked. Rule, lists, order and limits unchanged, kept by replay::readiness (chains, shared parents, cycles, done and disputed statuses, epics, claims, scopes, 80 random graphs) and commands::shared_readiness. A chain of 4,000 issues is judged in 1.8 ms where the lists took 1.74 s; bead ready there 2.05 -> 0.037 s, at 16,000 37.0 -> 0.149 s (cargo xtask timing --ready N; REVIEWING §2, FINDINGS Z04, GUARANTEES, CHANGELOG). ./check.sh green (892 passed, 3 skipped); Codex review of be67b21..6abf4ea found no defects. On local main at 6abf4ea, not pushed. Follow-up roll-lqjj.22 filed for the usage text omission noticed on the way.

Every shown issue's dependents are found at once: State::dependents_of (crates/beadroll-core/src/view/dependents.rs) reads every issue's edges once for all the issues a command names, keeping and sorting only the edges naming one of them by uid text, and State::detail_with lists each one's; bead show, update, claim and takeover make it once a command. State::detail of one issue is still one pass, comparing targets with its uid instead of hashing (half the old lookup's time), and a lookup from another state is never used. Dependents, their order, detail order, duplicate ids and ISSUE_NOT_FOUND where it stands are unchanged, kept by replay::dependents (60 random graphs among the cases, against detail alone and the old reading, member for member) and commands::shared_dependents (also green against the base binary). timing --details N: all details 20/49/95 ms at 4k/8k/16k vs 0.49/1.92/8.87 s each alone; lookup 3.0/8.1/17.0 ms vs 0.67/3.42/18.4 s; bead show of all 4,000 0.85 -> 0.13 s, 8,000 3.26 -> 0.28 s, same bytes (REVIEWING §2, FINDINGS Z05, GUARANTEES, CHANGELOG). ./check.sh green (905 passed, 3 skipped); Codex review of 6abf4ea..8683332 found no defects. On local main at 8683332, not pushed.

fields.description: Review 16 is a performance follow-up review of 4d7e03e..8683332 (roll-lqjj.15 to roll-lqjj.20). It found no correctness bug in that range and seventeen findings, ids X01 to X17: quadratic work left one step away from what the range fixed (bead blocked's lists, the blocked flag of several details, renamed copies), and where a command's time now goes (a projection switched off for good by one integrity entry, cache files fsynced, repeated projection decodes in online writes, per-attempt-file passes, journal-loading commands, show's git processes per closed issue, teardown, discovery's gits), plus guards and two design questions. This issue records the report under docs/reviews/ and a Review 16 section in docs/FINDINGS.md with every X row open; each fix lands under its own child issue and pull request, which sets its rows.
fields.acceptance_criteria: docs/reviews/2026-10-15-16-claude-performance-follow-up.md holds the report: what was checked and how, each finding with its evidence and measurement, ranked; docs/FINDINGS.md has a Review 16 section (ids X) with X01-X17 as open rows; the fix issues and their pull requests are named; docs only, the baseline's hygiene tests pass.
fields.title: Record review 16: its report and the X rows of the findings ledger

fields.description: X01: bead blocked builds each held issue's list with State::open_blockers (crates/beadroll/src/commands/queries.rs:28), each walking the issue's ancestry, so a deep hierarchy costs issues x depth: a held chain of 16,000 takes 43.2 s and of 4,000 2.05 s. X02: show, update, claim and takeover of several issues judge each detail's blocked with State::is_blocked (crates/beadroll-core/src/view.rs:146): show of every issue of that chain takes 28.7 s. Z04 left the lists where they are printed and Z05's probe had no parents, so neither saw this. X12: sort_for_listing allocates a String per comparison (4.3 ms against 3.1 ms for 20,000 issues). A prototype (blocked-lists.patch: Tarjan over the not-done parent graph, inherited sets shared; one Readiness for several details) makes the chain's blocked 0.26 s and show 0.62 s with byte-identical output. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: bead blocked lists every held issue's blockers in one pass over issues and edges plus the size of what it lists, equal for every issue to open_blockers (keys in key order), on deep chains, lattices, merged parent cycles, done and disputed ancestors and targets, epics, scopes and random graphs; several details share one readiness judgement and State::detail of one issue is unchanged; listing sorts without allocating; outputs byte-identical; xtask timing --ready measures the lists both ways; docs and ledger rows X01, X02, X12.
fields.title: List every held issue's blockers at once, and judge readiness once for several details

fields.description: X03: replay renames a copy whose key another machine minted too by State::free_key, which builds claimed_keys(), a set of every issue's key and every key an import waits for, once per copy (crates/beadroll-core/src/state.rs:275): two machines importing the same 8,000-record export offline, then syncing, rename 8,000 copies, and the second machine's sync takes 6.6 s and a cold replay 4.7 s, against 1.15 s for the same creates with nothing renamed. The awaiting index of roll-lqjj.18 already lists every awaited key: with by_key and that index asked per candidate (free-key.patch), 2.7 s and 1.1 s. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: free_key asks of each candidate whether an issue has it or an import waits for it, without collecting every key; the keys chosen are unchanged, which tests show against claimed_keys on replayed states and histories with renames and waiting imports; a probe measures a replay renaming N copies against its control; docs and ledger row X03.
fields.title: Find a renamed copy's key by lookups rather than by collecting every key for each copy

fields.description: X08: bead show answers each closed issue's merged with merged_into_default (crates/beadroll-store/src/place.rs:43), about five gits per issue, the default branch resolved again each time: 100 closed issues take 4.1 s and 1,000 29.8 s; resolved once and asked together (merged-batch.patch), 80 ms and 131 ms, output byte-identical. X14: where.commit comes from any machine's event and reaches git unchecked: a NUL fails show of that issue with IO, a leading '-' is read as an option, revision expressions such as HEAD~1 or :/regex are evaluated. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: show resolves the default branch's refs once a command and asks each distinct commit once, in a fixed number of git processes for the hex commits bead records; merged is unchanged for merged, unmerged, missing and empty commits and issues named twice (a test of several closed issues passes before and after); a NUL or a leading '-' never reaches git as an argument and answers unknown; whether a commit that is not hex should answer unknown is decided and recorded in docs/REVIEWING.md section 2; docs and ledger rows X08, X14.
fields.title: Ask git whether closed issues are merged once a command, and keep journal text out of git's options

fields.description: X05: write_atomic always fsyncs (crates/beadroll-store/src/fs.rs:91), so the command after every write flushes the projection and appends to its text file with an fsync, as the journal is. Both are caches bead rebuilds whenever they are missing, cut or damaged, and every part is read against its sum. Unflushed (floor.patch), the read after a write takes 9.5 ms instead of 39.1 ms on 300 issues and 42 ms instead of 74 ms on 5,000 (medians, interleaved); a write cycle about halves on Linux. The journal, attempts, pending files, meta.json and the memo, which has no sum, stay fsynced. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: The projection and its text file are written whole and atomically without fsync, every other store file as before; a test or reasoning recorded in docs/REVIEWING.md section 2 (the durability bullet) says why a crash can only cost a replay: a lost, cut, zeroed or stale projection or text file is never read as current; failpoints atomic-write and atomic-written still fire for them; before/after of a write followed by a read; docs and ledger row X05.
fields.title: Write the projection and its text file without fsync: both are checksummed caches

fields.description: X04: Projection::extend declines whenever the state holds any integrity entry (crates/beadroll-core/src/projection.rs:116, projection/extend.rs:240), so one newer bead's operation in a rolling upgrade, a quarantined duplicate or a copied machine identity makes every later write replay the whole journal, and close, reopen and delete replay once per issue (transition.rs:73 reads tx.state() after every emit, tx.rs:199): 60 closes on 4,000 issues take 10.3 s instead of 0.07 s. An experiment (open-with-integrity.patch) that lets the projection extend whenever nothing is pending, with unknown operations and invalid payloads added to the differential test, matched replay on 13,088 extensions over 400 seeds, and the same close took 0.074 s; quarantined duplicates, chain breaks, unreadable lines and refused takeovers were not in it. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: The projection extends past integrity entries when nothing is pending and every new event applies, only if the differential test against replay, extended with every kind of integrity entry (unknown operation, invalid payload, unreadable line, quarantined duplicate, chain break, refused takeover), passes on many seeds; otherwise the narrowest rule that does; close, reopen and delete of M issues on a projection that cannot extend replay at most once, not M times; the decision is recorded in docs/REVIEWING.md section 2; before/after with inert.sh; docs and ledger row X04.
fields.title: Keep extending the projection past an integrity entry, and read the state once per transition

fields.description: X06: an online write decodes the projection four or five times: Tx::new, the command's answer, synchronise's known_renames (crates/beadroll-sync/src/synchronise.rs:136, to count renames), Link::merge's own-chain check (link/merge.rs:117) and synchronise's final view, which publish_to drops (synchronise.rs:427). update, dep, claim and release clone the whole state to read it while emitting (update.rs:169, dep.rs:168, ownership.rs:59, 257). At 20,000 imported issues an online comment takes 1.10 s against 0.30 s offline, a state clone 49 ms. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: An online write and a sync decode the projection as few times as they need (at most once per merge round plus once for the command), no command clones the whole state to emit, the Synced report is made only for a caller that reads it, renames are counted without a decode of their own; protocol behaviour, outputs and receipts unchanged; ./check.sh --stress green; before/after of online writes and a no-op sync; docs and ledger row X06.
fields.title: Decode the projection once per online write, and stop cloning the whole state

fields.description: X07: attempt files are never compacted (a decision), and a command pays per attempt file several times: held() stats each in current() and again in appended() (crates/beadroll-store/src/projection.rs:160, :411), the link stats them for the memo and blobs, meta.json's published map (one entry per file) is parsed two to four times and cloned, and the memo once more: with 92,000 attempt files list takes 1.04 s against 0.19 s, an online write 6.1 s, a no-op sync 4.5 s (461,000 statx). X13: appended() and load_listed list claims through the shared listing, which can reuse the listing current() took before any segment was read, when the directory's identity did not move (kernels before 6.13): a record that builds on an attempt landed in that tick is then pending for one read. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Each attempt file is stat-ed at most once a command and meta.json parsed once, outputs and published trees unchanged; attempts are listed afresh once the segments are read (a test, failing before, with the simulated same-tick listing of review-correctness-tests.patch or a failpoint); before/after on the ownership-heavy timing store (timing --read N --ownership); ./check.sh --stress green; docs and ledger rows X07, X13.
fields.title: Pay for each attempt file once a command, and list claims after the segments are read

fields.description: X09: bead log loads the whole journal, clones it and replays it (crates/beadroll/src/commands/history.rs:29-32) to name keys; info loads it for counts and the frontier (info.rs:24); machines for per-machine totals and last times (history.rs:132). At 20,000 issues: log 1.47 s, info 1.24 s, machines 0.91 s, where list takes 0.26 s. The projection holds the state, the frontier, every event id and each machine's journal length. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: log takes keys from the projection's state and replays nothing; info and machines read what the projection (or the memo) already holds and load the journal only for what they cannot answer otherwise; every output byte-identical (tests); before/after at 20,000 issues; docs and ledger row X09.
fields.title: log, info and machines without loading and replaying the whole journal

fields.description: X10: a reading command frees its whole state before the process exits: at 200,000 events, decoding takes about 100 ms and freeing about 50 to 85 ms; kept until exit (floor.patch), list takes 0.154 s instead of 0.205 s, show 0.154 s instead of 0.203 s. A write frees the transaction's whole projection inside locked() (crates/beadroll-sync/src/tx.rs:252), so other commands wait for the store lock while memory is freed. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: The state a command answers from is kept until exit (the CLI only; libraries free as before), never two at once, so heap peaks do not rise (cargo xtask bead); the write's transaction is freed after the lock is released; outputs unchanged; before/after of list, show and a write at 200,000 events; docs and ledger row X10.
fields.title: Keep a command's state until exit, and free a write's projection after the lock

fields.description: X11: every command starts git config and git rev-parse together, then git cat-file --batch for the committed .beadroll.json (crates/beadroll-store/src/discover.rs:56) only once both have answered, about 1.4 ms a git process on Linux and more on macOS, a few ms of every command on a small tracker (bead list takes 6.2 ms on one issue). Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Where discovery needs the committed .beadroll.json, its cat-file starts with the other two and its answer is used only where the tree has no .beadroll.json, every answer and error unchanged (the hardening tests of discovery and tracked configuration); the git processes a command starts and its wall time before/after on a small tracker; docs and ledger row X11.
fields.title: Start discovery's three gits together

fields.description: X15: the tests of roll-lqjj.15 to .20 compare answers, and timings never gate, so a change that makes any of them quadratic again passes every test: State::readiness asked issue by issue, dependents found per detail, the awaiting index scanned, finish_some relabelling everything, import planning scanning the batch. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Each guarded algorithm has a test that fails when its work grows with the square of its input and passes with margin otherwise, deterministic (counted work, not wall time) or, where only time can say, a ratio of N to 8N with generous bounds run by the nightly workflow in release; the decision is recorded (xtask's 'timings never gate' invariant and docs/REVIEWING.md section 2); docs and ledger row X15.
fields.title: Guard the cost of Z01-Z05 and X01-X03 against regressing to quadratic

fields.description: X16 (design, no pull request yet): at 200,000 events a reading command decodes about 100 ms of state whatever it prints. A decoded issue keeps each short field twice (its fields and its register: title, priority, assignee, status), each dependency target as a 36-byte uuid string with a two-string metadata object, and every named event's causes, which only extension uses (about a quarter of the decode). An outline part (what list, ready, blocked and prime read), typed edge targets with interned kinds, and short fields shown from their registers as long fields are (roll-lqjj.10) would let a read cost what it prints. Related: roll-lqjj.21. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: A design recorded here with measurements (decode phases, bytes per part) and the chosen order of steps, each a change of projection::ENCODING only, format 1 unchanged.
fields.title: Reading commands decode the whole state: an outline part, typed edges, short fields kept once

fields.description: X17 (design, no pull request yet): after each write the next command extends the projection by a record (0.3 ms at 200,000 events) and then encodes and writes all of it (96 ms, 19 MB) after a decode with its index (136 ms); the ids of every event (3.2 MB at 200,000) and the knowledge are rewritten each time. Options: extend from the journal's tail without saving until the tail is long, save only the parts that changed, keep the event ids out of what is rewritten. Evidence and measurements: /home/aa/.cache/beadroll-review16/ (review-notes.md, sweep-notes.md), the review 16 report once roll-lqjj.23 lands.
fields.acceptance_criteria: A design recorded here with measurements of a write cycle by phase and the chosen approach.
fields.title: Every write cycle re-encodes and rewrites the whole projection

data.text: PR: https://github.com/bpcakes/beadroll/pull/6 (docs only: the report, the Review 16 section of FINDINGS.md with X01-X17 open, the review count in REVIEWING.md). The fix PRs are based on its branch review-16-findings and set their own rows.

Implemented: write_cache_parts (fs.rs) for projection + texts start/append; tests: texts lost behind projection, every projection x text-file crash pairing, failpoints on both files. strace confirms no fsync of either file. Measured (30 interleaved runs, write then show): 300 issues read 39.4->9.5 ms, 5000 issues 72.1->46.4 ms; timing --read 1000 write 29->20 ms. Docs in REVIEWING durability bullet, GUARANTEES, FINDINGS X05, CHANGELOG. check.sh running; PR next.

Implemented on branch history-from-the-projection: log takes keys from view_outline after reading the journal (no replay, no clone); info and machines answer from projection(ws) alone. The projection lacked each machine's latest event (machines' last_event: the greatest id, not the last record, since clocks go back), so it now keeps it beside the journal lengths (projection::ENCODING 5). 20k issues (setup.sh, release, best of 5, shared machine): info 1.16->0.21 s, machines 0.88->0.22 s, log 1.37->1.24 s (still reads the journal for causal order, as asked). Outputs byte-identical there; new black-box test passes on the old bead too. timing --read 200000 extended with log/info/machines; running.

Approach: beadroll-core counts work in its own tests (work::tally, cfg(test) only; Edge via Issue::deps/dep_tags and State::children, Relabel, Index, Waiting via state::awaited and the Awaiting index, Key via import id_of/target); work::tests::{import,finished,awaiting,edges} guard at 250 vs 2000, fail above 16x. xtask timing::growth (ignored, nightly release, --test-threads 1) times what counts cannot see (import scans, inline waiting-key reads, ids vector), fail above 24x. 14 counted and 3 timed mutations each fail their guard. X01-X03 guards written and verified failing on main / passing with the prototype patches; to be added when those land (PR text has them).

Implemented on branch one-decode-per-online-write (68fb442 code, 5618fd2 docs, on top of origin/review-16-findings): write's sync makes no report/renames count; merge keeps its projection (Link::merged) for the Synced report and the ownership round's Tx (Tx::on); reporting sync counts renames from a pre-merge projection reused when the merge writes nothing; update answers from writing_state; Tx::lend replaces the 4 State clones. Reads at 20k issues: comment/update/close/create/dep add/claim 4/5/4/4/4/3 -> 2, no-op sync 3 -> 1. Running ./check.sh --stress.

PR: https://github.com/bpcakes/beadroll/pull/11 (based on #6). X01-X03 guard code is in the PR body, verified failing on main and passing with the prototype patches; add with/after roll-lqjj.24 and roll-lqjj.25.

Rule found by extending the differential test with every integrity kind (projection/tests/flawed.rs): open = nothing pending AND no takeover refused for naming an id no event has (a later event with that id changes its refusal reason: 'not a claim on this issue' -> 'had not seen'; reproduced at seeds 182, 90); and extend declines a batch carrying an id an integrity entry names (a record found only in another machine's journal is settled anew once its own record arrives; reproduced at seed 44). Both narrowings proven needed by removing each. transition decides every issue from one state, one read after emits.
